private_lines.Tom: You fixed the sticking side gate at home before nine, planing the bottom edge and oiling the hinges. Your partner brought you a bacon sandwich at eleven, and you ate it on the back step in the thin sunshine. By lunchtime you had printed the Horsforth cable schedule and tucked it behind the van's sun visor.

private_lines.Chloe: You ran slowly round Roundhay Park before the cold got worse, and a spaniel kept trying to join in until its owner gave up calling it back. Afterwards you bought a bag of clementines and a small Christmas tree that you'll have to carry up three flights of stairs.

private_lines.Hannah: You slept until nearly seven, then spent the morning on the washing and eggs on toast by the window. In the afternoon you walked up through Hyde Park in thin sunshine and carried a small fir home from the stall outside the Co-op, setting it in the corner of the front room. The rest of the afternoon went on untangling last year's fairy lights, and you left the Thursday deadline alone.

private_lines.Dev: You spent the afternoon at the kitchen table marking Year 11 mock papers and got through about half before the light went. Around four the neighbour's cat came back over the garden wall, so you gave it the end of the ham. You still need to print the parents' evening sheets before Thursday.

private_lines.Tom: You and your partner walked round Roundhay Park in the afternoon, past the lake, where a spaniel kept lunging at the ducks and missing. Back home you spent an hour on the loft's test certificates and paperwork at the kitchen table, then made beans on toast while the light went.

private_lines.Chloe: Back in Chapel Allerton, you carried the tree up three flights and dropped the clementines on the second landing, so one rolled down to the ground floor and into the neighbour's bin. You got the tree into its stand by mid-afternoon, then spent the evening setting your alarm for 5:50 and sorting out what you need for Friday's long shift.
